strengths: Strong practical efficiency gains: achieves comparable performance to BioEmu with ~10x less MD training data and ~8x less compute, which is significant for practitioners
Comprehensive multi-faceted evaluation: equilibrium sampling, long-timescale dynamics, temperature-dependent kinetics, and cryptic binding pockets; goes beyond single-metric benchmarking
Physically meaningful behavior: learned temperature-dependent rates exhibit non-Arrhenius behavior consistent with complex protein free energy landscapes
Solid reproducibility infrastructure: detailed hyperparameters (Table 2), sampling procedures (Tables 3-4), algorithms (Algorithms 1-3), and extensive supplementary visualizations
Systematic ablation studies: proper evaluation of different conditioning signals (pLM, structure, LLM) under identical experimental conditions
Clear presentation: well-motivated, generally well-written with informative figures and comprehensive appendices
weaknesses: Critical unexplained negative result: LLM-derived annotations decrease performance (MAE: 0.938→1.066, RMSE: 1.213→1.346, Coverage: 0.655→0.570), directly contradicting the paper's central narrative about auxiliary information; dismissed with vague speculation rather than investigation
Overstated claims on cryptic binding pockets: PLaTITO-Big fails to sample apo state in 2 of 4 cases (~50% failure rate); authors acknowledge limited metastability but claim SOTA anyway

Systematic timescale underestimation: model predicts 5-7x faster folding/unfolding rates than MD (5.5 vs 27 μs folding). While variational principle explains underestimation, the large magnitude is concerning and no solution proposed
Limited scope: max 80 residues tested (training ≤200); Cα-only coarse-graining misses side-chain dynamics; only 12 fast-folding proteins; no protein complexes, ligands, or varied force fields tested

Unfair efficiency comparison with BioEmu: BioEmu trained on additional 131k AFDB structures + 502k ΔG measurements, while PLaTITO leverages large pretrained models (ESM, Proteina, DeepSeek); 10x efficiency claim doesn't control for external data
Incremental novelty: primarily adds pLM embeddings to existing ITO framework (Diez et al. 2025a); limited methodological innovation; structure/LLM embeddings exploratory but unsuccessful
Incomplete ablation on pLM: no analysis of which ESM features help; doesn't identify what linguistic/structural properties enable transfer
Limited baseline comparisons: only compared to BioEmu; missing comparisons to other transfer learning approaches (e.g., fine-tuned Timewarp)
Insufficient uncertainty quantification: most figures lack error bars; uncertainty only in Table 1 via MSM posterior sampling

Temperature extrapolation not validated: Trp-cage requires adjustment from 290K (MD) to 310K (TITO) as outside training range (320-450K); unclear if this reflects proper generalization or distribution shift
No code availability stated and some proprietary data, limiting reproducibility
Markovian properties not empirically validated despite acknowledging lack of formal guarantees
Missing analysis: no investigation of what protein properties enable/prevent transfer; no systematic failure mode analysis beyond cryptic pockets

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across multiple protein systems and metrics (free energy landscapes, kinetics, cryptic pockets)
Practical efficiency gains: 8× reduction in compute vs BioEmu and 4× less MD data while achieving competitive performance
Thorough experimental work with clear presentation, detailed appendices, and reproducibility-supporting information
Honest discussion of limitations including coarse-graining, lack of theoretical guarantees, and systematic time-scale underestimation
Systematic ablation study investigating different conditioning signals (sequence, structure, LLM annotations)
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily combines existing ITO and flow matching techniques with standard pre-trained embedding conditioning—no fundamental algorithmic innovations
Modest improvements from claimed main contribution: pLM embeddings provide only ~11% improvement on key metrics, while structural embeddings sometimes outperform pLM variants despite title emphasis
LLM-derived annotations harm performance (PLaTITO+Struct+LLM worse than PLaTITO+Struct), contradicting narrative about auxiliary conditioning improving generalization; explanation is dismissive
Severe systematic time-scale bias: model predicts folding 5× and unfolding 2× faster than MD; invoking variational principles post-hoc doesn't validate for kinetic applications
Trp-cage 'out-of-distribution' evaluation is problematic: training range 320–450 K, reference MD 290 K, but authors sample at 310 K to stay in-distribution, undermining OOD generalization claims
Marginal improvement on cryptic binding pockets: only succeeds in 1 of 3 failure cases vs BioEmu; authors acknowledge model fails to form metastable basins
Incomplete baseline comparisons: only BioEmu compared; DeepJump mentioned but not directly evaluated; limited engagement with other recent transfer operator methods

Unfair data efficiency narrative: BioEmu uses different auxiliary data (131k AFDB structures, 502k ΔG measurements); comparison conflates different modalities rather than controlling for like-for-like data
Coarse-grained Cα-only representation severely limits applicability for ligand binding, allostery, and specificity—fundamental constraint acknowledged but not adequately addressed
Statistical significance of improvements unclear: large error bars reported without formal testing; some differences may be within noise margins

strengths: Strong empirical results: achieves state-of-the-art equilibrium sampling performance (MAE 0.824 vs. BioEmu 1.110) with significantly lower data and compute requirements (56 ms vs. 216 ms training data; 1,100 vs. 9,216 GPU hours)
Novel and well-motivated insight about leveraging protein language model embeddings to improve data efficiency and out-of-distribution generalization for molecular dynamics surrogates

Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks: equilibrium sampling on 12 fast-folding proteins, long-timescale dynamics, temperature-dependent kinetics, and cryptic binding pockets with proper ablation studies

Physically meaningful learned dynamics: model recovers non-Arrhenius temperature dependence consistent with complex energy landscapes, demonstrating learning of realistic dynamics beyond pattern matching
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, training/sampling algorithms, transparent architectural choices, and reference to public datasets enable community adoption
Honest limitations discussion: clearly articulates scope limitations (coarse-grained representation, lack of formal guarantees, limited chemical space generalization) without over-claiming
weaknesses: Limited core methodological novelty: primary contribution is concatenating different embedding representations to existing ITO framework—more of an engineering contribution than a fundamental algorithmic advance

Incomplete analysis of auxiliary representations: structure embeddings provide only modest improvements (MAE 0.949→0.938) with online computational overhead; LLM-derived annotations actually decrease performance (MAE 0.938→1.066) with minimal analysis of why

Narrow scope and generalization: limited to small proteins (≤80 residues), coarse-grained Cα-only representation ignores critical side-chain dynamics, only 12 fast-folding proteins tested (atypical subset), and cryptic binding pocket evaluation limited to 4 systems with PLaTITO-Big failing in 2/4 cases
Insufficient baseline comparisons: only compared against BioEmu; missing direct comparisons with TITO (Diez et al. 2025a) and DeepJump (Costa et al. 2025b) which also use mdCATH dataset

Systematic underestimation of timescales suggests model may not fully capture transition kinetics: predicted folding MFPT ~5.5 µs vs. MD ~27 µs (4.8× discrepancy), with limited discussion of implications for applications
Temperature extrapolation issues: Trp-cage reference MD at 290 K is outside training range (320-450 K), undermining out-of-distribution generalization claims; sampled at 310 K instead

Weak cryptic binding pocket results: PLaTITO-Big recovers apo state in only 1 additional case compared to BioEmu baseline failure cases; fails to form metastable basins in 2 systems with vague explanation about 'energetic separation'

Missing important ablations: no ablation testing temperature-only conditioning, insufficient analysis of how much improvement comes from model capacity (3M→19M) vs. larger ESM embeddings (300M→6B), limited sensitivity analysis for pretrained model choice

strengths: Strong practical impact with ~10-fold reduction in training data and compute compared to BioEmu while achieving superior performance across metrics (MAE: 0.824 vs 1.110)

Comprehensive and well-designed evaluation across multiple dimensions (equilibrium sampling, timescale dynamics, temperature-dependent kinetics, cryptic binding pockets) with proper train-test splits and ablation studies
Reproducible work with complete algorithmic details, hyperparameters, and thorough experimental documentation; code availability promised
Scientifically meaningful results including recovery of non-Arrhenius kinetics consistent with complex protein folding landscapes
Systematic ablation studies demonstrating pLM benefits across multiple families (ESM2, ESMC) and model capacities (1M-100M parameters), indicating robust insights
Honest treatment of limitations in Section 6; clear discussion of coarse-graining constraints, lack of formal guarantees, and generalization boundaries
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily incremental engineering of adding pLM embeddings to existing TITO framework rather than fundamental methodological innovation

Lacks mechanistic insight into why pLM embeddings improve performance—could be capturing evolutionary conservation, structural propensities, or other features; this black-box behavior limits understanding and reproducibility
LLM-derived annotations component degrades performance (MAE 1.066 vs 0.938) despite being presented as a contribution; minimal analysis of failure suggests incomplete understanding of own method

Failure cases incompletely addressed: cryptic binding pockets recover apo state in only 1 of 3 baseline failures (not all); systematic timescale underestimation (5.5 vs 27 μs for folding) acknowledged but not investigated

Unfair baseline comparison: BioEmu trained on additional external data (131k AFDB structures, 502k experimental ΔG measurements) beyond mdCATH; hyperparameters inconsistent across models (different batch sizes, learning rates, steps in Table 2)

Restricted applicability: 200-residue limit excludes biologically relevant proteins; coarse-grained Cα-only representation ignores side-chain dynamics critical for ligand binding and allosteric regulation; no pathway to all-atom extension
Temperature generalization limited: Trp-cage temperature adjusted outside training range (290K→310K for 320-450K range); training on narrow temperature window may limit portability

Overstated claims: 'state-of-the-art' claimed despite failures in 2 of 4 cryptic pocket cases; 'improves out-of-distribution generalization' tested only on similar fast-folding proteins, not diverse protein classes

strengths: Significant practical improvements in data efficiency (10× reduction vs BioEmu) and computational cost (8× fewer GPU hours)
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple metrics including equilibrium sampling, long-timescale dynamics, temperature-dependent kinetics, and binding pockets
Thorough ablations on pLM families and model capacities (Appendices D.3-D.4) demonstrating generality of benefits
Recovery of physically meaningful non-Arrhenius temperature dependence consistent with rugged energy landscapes
High reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, algorithms, and architectural specifications in appendices
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of free energy landscapes and comparative results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is adding pre-trained pLM embeddings to existing TITO framework (Diez et al., 2026); all components (flow matching, Proteina transformer, pLM embeddings) are borrowed
Lack of mechanistic understanding: paper does not investigate *why* pLM embeddings improve performance or what thermodynamic information they encode; no analysis of which features matter

Contradictory auxiliary signal results: LLM-derived annotations (Section 5.2, Table 1) significantly hurt performance (MAE 1.066 vs 0.938 for PLaTITO+Struct), yet this failure is not explained or investigated, undermining the premise of beneficial auxiliary signals
Systematic timescale underestimation of 2-5× (MFPT_PLaTITO = 5.5±0.9 vs 27±8 μs); attributed vaguely to variational principle with unsubstantiated claim that further scaling would help
Mixed results on cryptic binding pockets with 2-3 failure cases out of 4 systems (Appendix D.7); unclear distinction between claimed 'energetic separation' and incomplete mode coverage
Confounded ablations: transition from TITO to PLaTITO involves simultaneous changes to batch size, transformer layers, and embedding dimensions; unclear if gains come from pLM signals or architecture
Narrow scope limited to proteins ≤200 residues with coarse-grained (Cα-only) representation missing side-chain effects; no path to larger systems or all-atom modeling

Limited baseline comparisons: BioEmu designed for equilibrium sampling (not dynamics); ConfDiff and Str2Str only in appendix; no comparison with fine-tuning or other transfer learning approaches in MD
Small test set: only 12 fast-folding proteins; train-test separation assessed only by sequence similarity (40% threshold), not structural similarity
Incomplete code release: GitHub URL in manuscript is truncated and non-functional

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks (equilibrium sampling, long-timescale dynamics, temperature-dependent rates, cryptic pockets) with rigorous out-of-distribution testing
Demonstrates substantial practical improvements: 10× less training data and computational cost compared to BioEmu baseline while achieving state-of-the-art performance
Well-motivated incorporation of protein language model embeddings with consistent improvements shown across different pLM families and model scales (Appendix D.3-D.4)
Technical soundness: Conditional flow matching framework is properly implemented and two-stage architecture design is elegant
Honest and comprehensive limitations discussion addressing theoretical gaps (no formal guarantees of detailed balance/Chapman-Kolmogorov consistency) and practical constraints
Strong reproducibility: Extensive architectural details, hyperparameters, algorithms, and sampling procedures provided with error bars across multiple runs
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily applies existing TITO framework (Diez et al., 2025) with pLM conditioning on a larger dataset rather than introducing new methods
Unfair baseline comparison: BioEmu trained on additional external data (131k AFDB structures + 502k ΔG measurements) beyond 56ms MD data; the '10× less data' claim requires qualification
LLM-derived annotations (Section 4.3-III) actually decrease performance (MAE 1.066 vs 0.938); this negative result lacks explanation and raises questions about component inclusion
Persistent failure modes: still fails on 2/3 cryptic binding pocket baseline cases; systematic underestimation of folding timescales (5.5 ± 0.9 μs vs 27 ± 8 μs MD reference)
Representation limitations: Cα-only coarse-grained approach ignores sidechains critical for ligand specificity and allosteric effects; applicability limited to ≤200 residue proteins in training
Temperature extrapolation concern: model trained on 320-450K range; test temperature adjusted from 290K to 310K for Trp-cage because original is outside training range
Incomplete code reference and proprietary test dataset: GitHub URL incomplete; fast-folding dataset available only upon request, limiting reproducibility
Non-equivariant architecture choice not justified: trade-offs versus equivariant approaches (SE(3)) remain unexplored; reasons for early structure embedding extraction (2 layers) not explained
